summary:
We built Mission Architect because space mission design is rarely taught for what it actually is: a chain of constant trade-offs. We wanted students to sit in the engineer’s seat, make those hard calls themselves, and see the consequences play out.

The game follows the real lifecycle of a space mission. You begin with the planning phase—setting science goals, plotting trajectories, staying under budget, and clearing each milestone with a simulated review board. Then comes hardware engineering. Adjusting sliders for fuel, engine thrust, solar panels, cooling radiators, and dish size instantly alters your power, thermal, and weight budgets while your spacecraft updates visual form on screen.

Launching is where design flaws catch up to you. Every turn throws real-world trouble your way—meteoroid impacts, power drops, dust storms, or jammed hardware. Skimp on power or overheat your payload, and your science yield suffers. A post-mission debrief breaks down performance system by system.

Destinations draw directly from NASA NSSDCA data for gravity, atmosphere, temperature, and solar flux. That’s why Mars demands a sky crane, lunar landers need pure engine thrust, and Titan’s thick sky makes flying effortless but beaming data home a struggle. Everything runs on real physics, from the rocket equation to inverse-square lighting.

Includes guided training, starter designs, three difficulty modes, auto-save, and instant browser play with no signup needed.
details:
Mission Architect is a browser-based simulator that teaches space mission engineering through real-world trade-offs. Rather than picking pre-built rockets, players balance mass, power, heat, communications, and budget across three core phases:

  • Plan: Set objectives, trajectory, payload, and budget for 7 destinations (ranging from Low Earth Orbit to a Titan rotorcraft) and clear a simulated review board.
  • Design: Configure spacecraft subsystems—propellant, thrust, solar panels, batteries, radiators, and antennas. Sliders dynamically update performance budgets and a live SVG model.
  • Fly & Debrief: Manage in-flight anomalies (power drops, dust storms, component failures) that impact science yields, followed by a system-by-system performance audit.

Technical & Pedagogical Highlights

  • Physics & NASA Data: Built on real NASA NSSDCA planetary factsheets and core equations ($v_e$, Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, entry heating, inverse-square signal and solar decay, thermal radiation).
  • Zero Friction: Plain HTML/CSS/JS with no frameworks, installs, or account setup required. Runs instantly in any browser with auto-saving, starter templates, and guided tutorials.
